en e-mail.explanation: "En e-mail" means "an email". To say it the short way, drop the "e-": "Jeg sender dig en mail" (I will send you an email).

en edderkop.explanation: "En edderkop" means "a spider". To say you fear spiders, use the plural: "Jeg er bange for edderkopper" (I am afraid of spiders).

en effekt.explanation: "En effekt" means "an effect". To say something does not work, say: "Det har ingen effekt" (It has no effect).

en efterforsker.explanation: "En efterforsker" means "an investigator". It comes from the verb "at efterforske" (to investigate): "Politiet efterforsker sagen" (The police are investigating the case).

en efterforskning.explanation: "En efterforskning" means "an investigation". It comes from the verb "at efterforske" (to investigate). To say it has begun, say: "Politiet har indledt en efterforskning" (The police have started an investigation).

en efterfølger.explanation: "En efterfølger" means "a successor". To say a film has a follow-up, use it for a sequel: "Filmen fik en efterfølger" (The film got a sequel).

en efterløn.explanation: "En efterløn" means "an early-retirement pension". It is a Danish scheme that people can pay into through an unemployment fund. It is built from "efter" (after) and "en løn" (a wage).

en eftermiddag.explanation: "En eftermiddag" means "an afternoon". To say something happens in the afternoon, use "om eftermiddagen" (in the afternoon): "Jeg træner om eftermiddagen" (I work out in the afternoon). To say "this afternoon", use "i eftermiddag": "Vi ses i eftermiddag" (See you this afternoon).

en eftermiddagskaffe.explanation: "En eftermiddagskaffe" means "an afternoon coffee". It is built from "eftermiddag" (afternoon) and "en kaffe" (a coffee). To invite someone over, say: "Kom forbi til eftermiddagskaffe" (Come by for afternoon coffee).

en efterskole.explanation: "En efterskole" means "a boarding school". It is a Danish school for students aged 14 to 18 that they choose to attend instead of the last years at a regular school. To say you go to one, use "på" (at): "Hun går på efterskole" (She goes to boarding school).

en efterårsdag.explanation: "En efterårsdag" means "a fall day". It is built from "efterår" (fall) and "en dag" (a day). To say something happens in the fall, use "i efteråret" (in the fall): "Bladene falder af træerne i efteråret" (The leaves fall from the trees in the fall).

en efterårsferie.explanation: "En efterårsferie" means "a fall break". In Denmark, schools have it as a week off in October. It is built from "efterår" (fall) and "ferie" (vacation).

en eg.explanation: "En eg" means "an oak". The "the" form "egen" is spelled like the word "egen" (own). To say "the oak", use it as a noun: "Egen står i haven" (The oak stands in the garden). To say "own", use it before a noun: "min egen bil" (my own car).

en egenskab.explanation: "En egenskab" means "a quality". It is built from "egen" (own) and the ending "-skab", as in "venskab" (friendship). To name a good quality, say: "en god egenskab" (a good quality).

en ejendom.explanation: "En ejendom" means "a property", as in a building with its land. To mark a place as owned by a private person, say: "Privat ejendom" (Private property).

en ejendomsmægler.explanation: "En ejendomsmægler" means "a real estate agent". The part "ejendom" means "property". The part "mægler" means "broker", as in "en børsmægler" (a stockbroker).

en ejer.explanation: "En ejer" means "an owner". It comes from "at eje" (to own). To name what someone owns, add "af" (of): "ejeren af huset" (the owner of the house).

en ejerbolig.explanation: "En ejerbolig" means "an owner-occupied home". It is built from "ejer" (owner) and "en bolig" (a home).

en ejerlejlighed.explanation: "En ejerlejlighed" means "a condominium". It is built from "ejer" (owner) and "en lejlighed" (an apartment).

en eks.explanation: "En eks" means "an ex". To say it in full, use "en ekskæreste" (an ex-boyfriend / ex-girlfriend): "Min ekskæreste bor i Odense" (My ex lives in Odense).

en eksamen.explanation: "En eksamen" means "an exam". To say you sit one, use "at tage eksamen" (to take an exam): "Hun tager eksamen i juni" (She takes her exam in June).

en eksaminator.explanation: "En eksaminator" means "an examiner". In a Danish oral exam, it is the teacher who asks the questions. Do not mix it up with "en censor" (an external examiner), who helps set the grade: "Censoren giver karakteren sammen med læreren" (The external examiner gives the grade together with the teacher).

en eksistens.explanation: "En eksistens" means "an existence". To call someone a shady person, use it for a person: "en tvivlsom eksistens" (a shady character).

en ekskursion.explanation: "En ekskursion" means "a field trip". Do not mix it up with "en udflugt" (a day out for fun): "Vi tog på udflugt til stranden" (We went on an outing to the beach).

en ekskæreste.explanation: "En ekskæreste" means "an ex". It is built from "eks" (former) and "en kæreste" (a boyfriend or girlfriend). The word "kæreste" is the same for men and women: "Hun er min kæreste" (She is my girlfriend).
